findings.paper_evidence: The surrounding LR setup takes epsilon and the beta scales positive and assumes u safely smaller than epsilon.
findings.translation_evidence: The run imposes neither positivity of epsilon, betaA, and betaB nor a relation between u and epsilon.
findings.impact: The theorem covers additional algebraically meaningful but nonstandard parameter choices. This does not remove any paper case but prevents reverse implication.

findings.translation_evidence: The outer binders admit all natural b and r, including b=0; incompatible r>b cases have no admissible runs.
findings.impact: The intended dimensional instances are preserved, while degenerate or impossible dimensions are added as trivial or vacuous cases.

findings.paper_evidence: The paper introduces an operation-level standard model and derives the generic matrix-product bound (2.7), which is the bound used in the proof.
findings.translation_evidence: The trace directly assumes the generic additive-error bound for each of the three matrix-product stages.
findings.impact: This is a conservative proof-level abstraction: every paper computation maps to a trace, while the translated trace space may also contain bounded perturbations not tied to a deterministic floating-point execution.

rationale: The blind translation preserves the matrices, shared rank, factor orientations, orthonormality placement, both parenthesizations, Frobenius norm, gamma constant, exact-versus-computed distinctions, both forward-error conclusions, and all higher-order terms. Its differences only broaden the parameter, dimension, and certified-trace domains. Consequently the translation entails the paper result but is not implied by the paper statement at the same scope, so it is accepted as faithful-stronger.
